summary: Return all matrix elements in clockwise spiral order.
mainInsight: Keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right). Walk top row left-to-right, right column top-to-bottom, bottom row right-to-left (if top <= bottom), left column bottom-to-top (if left <= right), shrinking the boundaries after each side. Check the boundary conditions before the last two sides to avoid duplicates for a single row or column.

approaches.name: Visited matrix with direction changes
approaches.summary: Turn right when the next cell is out of bounds or visited.

commonMistakes: Duplicating elements in single row/column cases

promptVariants: How do the four boundaries move during a spiral traversal?
What happens after the top row is finished?
options: top moves down after the top row, right moves left after the right column, etc.
All four boundaries move inward by one after each single side
Only the top and bottom boundaries ever move inward
The boundaries stay fixed while a visited set is used
cards.answer: top moves down after the top row, right moves left after the right column, etc.
cards.explanation: Each traversed side is removed from the remaining region.

incorrectOptionExplanations.All four boundaries move inward by one a: Only the boundary just traversed moves.

promptVariants: Why are checks needed before the bottom row and left column passes?
Which matrix shapes reveal the bug?
cards.answer: After shrinking top and right, the region may be a single row or single column; traversing the bottom row (or left column) would then repeat elements. Guarding with `top <= bottom` and `left <= right` prevents duplicates for inputs like a 1 x n or m x 1 matrix.
keyPoints: Region can collapse to a line
1 x n and m x 1 inputs
cards.explanation: Alternative: stop when the count equals m * n.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What does the spiral of [[1, 2, 3]] return?
What must the algorithm not do?
options: [1, 2, 3], without repeating elements on the way back
[1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1]: the bottom row is traversed backwards
[1, 3, 2]: the right column is read first
[]: a single row has no spiral
cards.answer: [1, 2, 3], without repeating elements on the way back
cards.explanation: Check top <= bottom before the bottom row.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1]: the bottom row is tr: A guard stops the bottom pass.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[1, 3, 2]: the right column is read firs: The top row is read left to right.
